title: Admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, and architect mock interviews
objectives: Scope each mock interview to an official credential or career page instead of leaked exam dumps or invented section weights.
Run separate admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, and architect mocks, each with its own checklist of what that loop is allowed to test.
Use Which Tool Help to choose Flow, Flow Approval Processes, Batch Apex, or Apex in a Flow mock, and define LWC as custom HTML elements built with HTML and JavaScript (CSS in the component bundle).
Treat Application Architect as a composite credential granted after four named prerequisites, and use Well-Architected Trusted, Easy, and Adaptable as the architect mock compass.
diagnostic_question: A hiring loop asks six original scenarios: users and automation, Apex custom interfaces, which automation tool, a Lightning panel next to Aura, an external system, and a Trusted/Easy/Adaptable design review. Which official page scopes each mock, and which two answers would mix lanes or invent exam weights?
definition: Admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, and architect mock interviews are timed practice loops scoped to official Salesforce credential and career pages—not exam dumps. An admin mock follows Platform Administrator and Admin career language (users, data, automation, extra platform features). A developer mock follows Platform Developer language (custom business logic and custom interfaces with Apex and Visualforce). A Flow mock starts from Which Tool Help. An LWC mock treats Lightning web components as custom HTML elements built using HTML and JavaScript, with CSS as the component stylesheet. An integration mock stays on interoperability and related Integration Architect language. An architect mock uses Well-Architected (Trusted, Easy, Adaptable) and treats Application Architect as granted only after its four prerequisites. ([Platform Administrator](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/platformadministrator); [Which Tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm); [LWC Get Started](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/get-started-introduction.html); [Application Architect](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/applicationarchitect); [Well-Architected](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail candidates who mix lanes: answering an admin mock with Apex trivia, treating LWC as Aura, skipping Which Tool in a Flow mock, or reciting unpublished Application Architect exam weights. CAREER-002 taught you to explain a solution; this lesson is how to practice the six distinct checklists without leaking exams or inventing percentages.
sixty_second_explanation: Treat each mock like a type-rated flight simulator: the admin aircraft, the developer aircraft, the Flow aircraft, the LWC glass cockpit, the integration airframe-to-airframe hookup, and the architect operations check all have different checklists. You do not fly a 737 sim with a Cessna card. Scope the admin mock to users, data, and automation; the developer mock to Apex and custom interfaces; the Flow mock to Which Tool; the LWC mock to HTML, JavaScript, and CSS; the integration mock to interoperability; the architect mock to Well-Architected after naming Application Architect prerequisites. Never recite unpublished exam weights.
deeper_explanation: The Platform Administrator credential page describes certified admins as Salesforce pros who help companies get more from the platform through additional features and capabilities. The Admin career path says admins manage users, data, and automation and keep systems secure and efficient. An admin mock therefore tests configuration, security, data, and automation judgment—not Apex class design. ([Platform Administrator](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/platformadministrator); [Admin career path](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/career-path/admin))

The Platform Developer credential page says certified developers develop and deploy custom business logic and custom interfaces using programmatic Lightning Platform capabilities, and can extend the platform with Apex and Visualforce. The Platform App Builder page is the declarative counterpart: design, build, and implement custom applications with declarative customization. Keep those two mocks separate. ([Platform Developer](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/platformdeveloperi); [Platform App Builder](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/platformappbuilder); [Developer career path](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/career-path/developer))

A Flow mock starts from Get Started Automating a Business Task with a Flow (Which Tool). Complementary tools on that article include Flow Approval Processes for multi-level approvals, Batch Apex when you must process more records than scheduled-triggered flows allow, Apex for CPU-intensive operations, and a custom invocable action that runs an Apex method with the InvocableMethod annotation. Original scenarios—not exam dumps. ([Which Tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm))

The LWC Get Started topic defines Lightning web components as custom HTML elements built using HTML and JavaScript; most of the code you write is standard JavaScript and HTML. LWC and Aura can coexist and interoperate on a page; when you have a choice, choose LWC. A typical component bundle also includes CSS for styling—do not claim the Get Started sentence lists CSS as the definition. ([LWC Get Started](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/get-started-introduction.html))

Application Architect is granted after four prerequisites succeed: Platform App Builder, Platform Data Architect, Platform Developer, and Platform Sharing and Visibility Architect. Certified Application Architects understand native features and are experts at modeling a role hierarchy, data, and sharing. Platform Integration Architect is listed as a related certification for end-to-end integration design—not as one of those four granting exams. Do not invent exam weights; these pages do not publish section percentages. ([Application Architect](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/en/credentials/applicationarchitect))

An architect mock uses Salesforce Well-Architected as the compass: Trusted solutions protect stakeholders, Easy solutions deliver value fast, Adaptable solutions evolve with the business. The Architect career path points to the Architecture Center, diagrams, and Decision Guides. ([Well-Architected](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview); [Architect career path](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/career-path/architect))

mental_model.analogy: Type-rated flight simulators: each aircraft (admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, architect) has its own checklist. You do not fly one sim with another aircraft's card.
useful_mapping: admin simulator → Platform Administrator / Admin career checklist: users, data, automation, extra features
developer simulator → Platform Developer checklist: Apex, Visualforce, custom business logic and interfaces
App Builder simulator → declarative custom apps, not the Apex type rating
Flow simulator → Which Tool Help as the preflight card for Flow vs approvals vs Batch Apex vs Apex
LWC glass cockpit → custom HTML element: HTML structure, JavaScript avionics, CSS paint
integration hookup → related Integration Architect / interoperability, not an Application Architect granting exam
architect operations sim → Well-Architected Trusted, Easy, Adaptable after the four Application Architect prerequisites
exam dump booklet → forbidden; original scenarios only
unpublished exam weights → not on these pages; do not invent percentages
where_it_breaks: Real credentials are not aircraft: Application Architect is granted after four completed exams, not after one long simulator session.
A hiring loop may mix lanes in one hour; you still answer with the matching checklist, not a blended fake syllabus.
LWC CSS is bundle styling; the official Get Started definition sentence names HTML and JavaScript, not CSS.
Well-Architected is a health compass, not a substitute for naming the four Application Architect prerequisites.

teach_back_prompt: Assign six original mock questions to admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, and architect lanes. Name the official page that scopes each one, say why Application Architect is composite, and state one thing you will not invent (exam weights or dumps).

review_schedule.prompt: From memory: Admin career manages users, data, and automation; PD uses Apex and Visualforce; AA is granted after four prerequisites.
Classify five signals into admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, or architect mock lanes using the decision table.
Explain the type-rated simulator analogy and where it breaks, including unpublished exam weights.
Walk a Flow Which Tool mock and an LWC HTML/JavaScript mock without notes.
Teach-back: six lanes, four Application Architect prerequisites, Well-Architected Trusted/Easy/Adaptable, no dumps.

telugu_glossary.telugu: సేల్స్‌ఫోర్స్ నిర్వాహకుడు — వినియోగదారులు, డేటా, ఆటోమేషన్ నిర్వహించే పాత్ర.
ప్లాట్‌ఫారమ్ డెవలపర్ — అపెక్స్ మరియు కస్టమ్ ఇంటర్‌ఫేస్‌లతో ప్రోగ్రామాటిక్ లాజిక్ నిర్మించే పాత్ర.
ఫ్లో — డిక్లరేటివ్ ఆటోమేషన్; ఏ టూల్ వాడాలో Which Tool సహాయం చూడండి.
లైట్నింగ్ వెబ్ కాంపోనెంట్ — HTML మరియు జావాస్క్రిప్ట్‌తో కస్టమ్ HTML ఎలిమెంట్; స్టైల్‌కు CSS కూడా ఉంటుంది.
ఇంటిగ్రేషన్ — వ్యవస్థల మధ్య అనుసంధానం; Application Architect మంజూరు జాబితాలోని నాలుగు పరీక్షలలో ఇది లేదు.
అప్లికేషన్ ఆర్కిటెక్ట్ — నాలుగు ముందస్తు సర్టిఫికేషన్లు పూర్తయిన తర్వాత మంజూరయ్యే సమ్మిళిత క్రెడెన్షియల్.
మాక్ ఇంటర్వ్యూ — అధికారిక క్రెడెన్షియల్ పేజీల పరిధిలో సాధన; పరీక్ష ప్రశ్నల కాపీ కాదు.
వెల్-ఆర్కిటెక్టెడ్ — నమ్మదగిన, సులభమైన, అనుకూలించగల పరిష్కారాల ఫ్రేమ్‌వర్క్.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I treat admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, and architect mocks as different type ratings. Each loop is scoped to an official credential or career page. I will not recite unpublished exam weights or dumps.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: Admin mocks follow users, data, and automation. Developer mocks follow Apex and custom interfaces. Flow mocks start at Which Tool. LWC is a custom HTML element of HTML and JavaScript, with CSS in the bundle. Integration is interoperability, not an Application Architect prerequisite. Architect mocks use Well-Architected after naming the four granting exams.

terminology.plain: The credential and mock lane for admins who extend the platform with features, not Apex-first design.
terminology.precise: Certified Platform Administrators help companies get more from the Salesforce Platform through additional features and capabilities. Career-path admins manage users, data, and automation.
terminology.example: Admin mock: how would you add a permission set and a record-triggered Flow for LAB_ Case escalation without writing Apex?
terminology.non_example: Asking the candidate to write a Visualforce controller in an admin mock.

terminology.boundary: Do not invent Platform Administrator exam section weights; the credential page does not publish them.

terminology.plain: The credential and mock lane for programmatic custom logic and custom interfaces.
terminology.precise: Certified Platform Developers develop and deploy custom business logic and custom interfaces using programmatic Lightning Platform capabilities and can extend the platform with Apex and Visualforce.
terminology.example: Developer mock: when would you use an Apex trigger versus a Flow, without quoting unofficial exam percentages?
terminology.non_example: A users-and-profiles admin quiz labeled as a developer mock.

terminology.non_example: A leaked exam item bank labeled as Which Tool practice.

when_to_use: Use an admin mock interview when the loop is Platform Administrator or Admin career work: users, data, automation, and extra platform features.
Use a developer mock interview when the interviewer tests programmatic custom business logic, Apex, Visualforce, or custom interfaces from the Platform Developer page.
Use a Flow mock when the question is which automation tool to pick; start from Which Tool Help before naming Flow, approvals, Batch Apex, or Apex.
Use an LWC mock interview when they want a custom Lightning UI: HTML and JavaScript custom elements, CSS in the bundle, Aura coexistence, prefer LWC.
Use an integration mock when the scenario is end-to-end interoperability, scoped to related Integration Architect language—not an Application Architect dump.
Use architect mock interviews when the loop is Well-Architected Trusted, Easy, Adaptable after you can name the four Application Architect prerequisites.
when_not_to_use: Do not run admin interviews from leaked exam dumps; scope mocks to the Platform Administrator credential and Admin career pages only.
Do not treat a developer mock as a recitation of unpublished Platform Developer exam weights; those interviews should use original Apex/interface scenarios.
Do not skip Which Tool in a Flow mock and jump to Apex for a simple multi-level approval the Help article maps to Flow Approval Processes.
Do not call LWC just Aura in interviews, and do not claim the Get Started definition sentence lists CSS as the official element recipe.
Do not invent Application Architect exam weights or list Integration Architect among the four granting prerequisites in an architect mock.
Do not collapse admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, and architect interviews into one unscoped quiz that mixes checklists.

She must practice original scenarios, not dumps, and must not invent exam weights.

steps: Open the Platform Administrator credential page and the Admin career path. Write three original admin mock questions about users, data, and automation. Map each question to a sentence on those pages.

Open Which Tool Help. For a two-level LAB_ PTO approval, a 600,000-contact overnight update, and a CPU-heavy discount, write which complementary tool the article maps, then turn each into a Flow mock prompt.

Open LWC Get Started. Explain aloud that Lightning web components are custom HTML elements built using HTML and JavaScript, that Aura can coexist, and that you choose LWC when you have a choice. State that CSS is the bundle stylesheet, not the Get Started definition sentence.

Open the Application Architect credential page. List the four prerequisites from the page. Write one architect mock using Well-Architected Trusted, Easy, and Adaptable, and one integration mock that does not treat Platform Integration Architect as a granting prerequisite.

Time a 30-second and a 2-minute answer for one prompt in the admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, and architect lanes. If a partner asks for exam section percentages, refuse and cite that these pages do not publish weights.

interview_questions.question: How do you scope an admin mock interview versus a developer mock?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: An admin mock follows Platform Administrator and Admin career pages: users, data, automation, and extra platform features. A developer mock follows Platform Developer: programmatic custom business logic and custom interfaces with Apex and Visualforce.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat them as different type ratings. For admin interviews I stay on configuration, security, data, and Flow-style automation the Admin career path names. For developer interviews I talk custom business logic and custom interfaces, Apex, and Visualforce from the Platform Developer page. I keep Platform App Builder as the declarative custom-app lane so I do not collapse it into Apex. I will not recite unpublished exam weights from either credential page.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Case escalation: admin mock designs permission sets and Flow; developer mock is asked when an Apex service is justified.
tradeoffs: Overlap exists between admin automation and developer Apex; name the lane before answering.
App Builder declarative skill is a third checklist, not a substitute for PD.
follow_ups: Where does Platform App Builder sit between those two mocks?
weak_answer_warnings: Answers Apex trivia in the admin mock

interview_questions.question: What is Application Architect, and how should an architect mock treat it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Application Architect is a composite credential granted after four prerequisites: Platform App Builder, Platform Data Architect, Platform Developer, and Platform Sharing and Visibility Architect. Architect mocks name that grant rule, then use Well-Architected.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would not pretend Application Architect is a single exam I crammed from dumps. The official page grants it when those four credentials succeed and describes experts in native features, role hierarchy, data, and sharing. My architect mock therefore starts by listing those four, then scores a design with Trusted, Easy, and Adaptable. I keep Platform Integration Architect as a related integration credential, not a fifth granting exam, and I do not invent section weights.
interview_questions.example: Architect mock: name the four prerequisites, then review LAB_ role hierarchy and sharing using Well-Architected Trusted.
tradeoffs: Hiring loops may still ask architect questions before you hold all four credentials.
Well-Architected is a compass, not a fake weight table.
follow_ups: Is Platform Integration Architect one of the four?
weak_answer_warnings: Lists Integration Architect as a granting prerequisite

interview_questions.question: Run a Flow mock: two-level LAB_ PTO approval, 600,000-contact update, and a CPU-heavy discount. Which tools and why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I open Which Tool Help first. Multi-level PTO approvals map to Flow Approval Processes. Volume beyond scheduled-triggered flows maps to Batch Apex. CPU-intensive discount math maps to Apex, or an InvocableMethod action if Flow must call it.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: A Flow mock is not 'always Flow' and not 'always Apex.' The complementary-tools table gives me the checklist: Flow Approval Processes for two-level PTO-style approvals; Batch Apex when I must process more records than scheduled-triggered flows allow, which Help illustrates with 600,000 contacts; Apex for CPU-intensive operations. If the business still wants a Flow entry point for that Apex, I mention a custom invocable action with InvocableMethod. I invent original LAB_ names, not dump items, and I do not attach fake exam weights to the answer.
interview_questions.example: Original prompts: LAB_ PTO two-level approval, overnight LAB_ Contact backfill of 600,000 rows, LAB_ discount engine.
tradeoffs: Flow Approval Processes versus Classic approvals may both appear in orgs; reverify Help.
Invocable Apex is an action, not a reason to skip Which Tool.
follow_ups: What would you say if someone asked for the Flow exam weight of that question?

interview_questions.question: An LWC mock: build a LAB_ Account panel next to an existing Aura component. What is LWC, and what do you choose?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: LWC are custom HTML elements built using HTML and JavaScript; most code is standard JS and HTML. CSS lives in the component bundle for styling. Aura can coexist on the page. When I have a choice, I choose LWC.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would not call LWC 'just Lightning Aura' or a Visualforce page. Official Get Started defines Lightning web components as custom HTML elements built using HTML and JavaScript. I mention CSS as the stylesheet in the bundle without claiming that definition sentence lists CSS. Admins and users see both LWC and Aura as Lightning components, and they can interoperate, so I can ship the new LAB_ Account panel as LWC beside the older Aura widget. If I can choose, I choose LWC. This mock stays on that definition; I do not invent compiler internals or exam weights.
interview_questions.example: c-lab-account-panel on the Account Lightning page beside an unmanaged Aura highlighter.
tradeoffs: Coexistence is not a mandate to rewrite Aura tonight.
CSS is bundle styling; quote HTML and JavaScript as the official definition.
follow_ups: What would a weak answer say about Aura versus LWC?
weak_answer_warnings: Says new UI must be Aura

interview_questions.question: How do you run an integration mock without confusing it with Application Architect?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I scope integration interviews to end-to-end interoperability. On the Application Architect page, Platform Integration Architect is a related credential for that work, not one of the four exams that grant Application Architect.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If the scenario is Salesforce talking to a warehouse or another system, I label it an integration mock. I can use Well-Architected Adaptable/Interoperability as the health language and the related Integration Architect blurb for 'assess the environment and design a scalable end-to-end integration.' I still will not list Integration Architect among App Builder, Data Architect, Platform Developer, and Sharing and Visibility Architect. I will not dump exam items or invent weights for either credential. If the loop later becomes an architect design review, I switch type ratings and name the four AA prerequisites.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ warehouse inventory sync: integration mock on Trusted security and Adaptable interoperability, not an AA grant checklist.
tradeoffs: Architect loops often include integration; still name which credential page you are using.
API family choice is a deeper INT lesson; do not fake Bulk limits here.
follow_ups: Where does Interoperability sit in Well-Architected?
weak_answer_warnings: Adds Integration Architect to the four AA prerequisites

interview_questions.question: Your study group is using a dump PDF and a blog of exam weights for admin and architect interviews. What do you change?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I stop the dump. I rebuild admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, and architect mocks from official credential, career, Which Tool, LWC, and Well-Architected pages, with original LAB_ scenarios and no invented weights.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Leaked items teach the wrong skill and are not the official pages this lesson uses. I replace the PDF with six type-rating cards. Admin card: Platform Administrator plus Admin career (users, data, automation). Developer card: Apex and custom interfaces. Flow card: Which Tool complementary tools. LWC card: HTML and JavaScript custom elements, CSS in the bundle, prefer LWC. Integration card: related Integration Architect, not an AA prerequisite. Architect card: four granting exams plus Trusted, Easy, Adaptable. If someone asks for percentages, I say these pages do not publish them.
interview_questions.example: Group retro: delete the dump, rewrite six original mocks, each citing one official URL from this topic.
tradeoffs: Official Trailhead practice tools, if present, are not third-party dumps.
Coaches must still time answers, not only collect URLs.
follow_ups: What is one original Flow mock you would write from Which Tool?

interview_questions.question: How would you structure a 30-minute mixed loop covering admin, Flow, LWC, and architect questions without blending checklists?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I would label each block as a type rating, open the matching official page in my notes, run original scenarios only, and switch checklists out loud when the interviewer changes lanes—including an architect block that names Application Architect prerequisites.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Minute 0–8 admin: users, data, automation from the Admin career and Platform Administrator pages. Minute 8–15 Flow: Which Tool complementary tools with original LAB_ prompts. Minute 15–22 LWC: HTML and JavaScript custom elements, CSS bundle, Aura coexistence, choose LWC. Minute 22–30 architect: list the four Application Architect prerequisites, then score Trusted, Easy, Adaptable. If integration appears, I mark it related, not a granting exam. I refuse dump items and unpublished weights the whole half hour. CAREER-002 still applies: explain to the audience in the room, but the facts come from the lane's official page.
interview_questions.example: Calendar invite with four labeled blocks and four official URLs pasted into the agenda.
tradeoffs: Real interviewers may not label lanes; you still switch checklists.
Thirty minutes cannot cover every complementary-tool row; pick two Flow signals.
follow_ups: Where would a developer Apex question fit if they added a fifth block?
weak_answer_warnings: One blended Salesforce monologue for all four blocks
Invented architect exam weights in the last eight minutes

interview_questions.question: Explain the type-rated flight-simulator analogy for these mocks and one place it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Each mock is a different aircraft checklist: admin, developer, Flow, LWC, integration, architect. You do not fly the architect sim with the admin card. It breaks because Application Architect is granted after four real credentials, not after one long simulator session.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The useful mapping is checklist discipline. Admin simulator: users, data, automation, extra features. Developer simulator: Apex, Visualforce, custom interfaces. Flow simulator: Which Tool. LWC glass cockpit: HTML, JavaScript, CSS in the bundle. Integration: airframe-to-airframe interoperability, related Integration Architect. Architect operations: Well-Architected Trusted, Easy, Adaptable. The analogy breaks when people think finishing the architect sim grants Application Architect—it does not; four prerequisites do. It also breaks if they treat unpublished exam weights as the aircraft manual; those pages do not publish weights, so original scenarios are the only legal flight plan.
interview_questions.example: Coach writes 'wrong aircraft' on the board when a candidate answers an admin mock with Visualforce.
tradeoffs: Mixed loops still happen; announce the type rating when you switch.
CSS is cockpit paint; official LWC definition sentence is HTML and JavaScript.
follow_ups: Give one more place the analogy breaks besides the composite grant.
weak_answer_warnings: Uses a generic mixed-lane story instead of type-rated checklists
Claims the sim grants Application Architect
